column3: The Hebrew says the earlier days “were before you”; BSB adds “long.”
The Hebrew explicitly says “to come” before “to take”; BSB leaves the coming implicit.
“These things” is supplied in BSB; the Hebrew simply has the passive “you were shown.”
The Hebrew suffixes are singular: “his seed after him,” following plural “your fathers.” It retains the image “by His face,” rendered as “by His presence” in BSB.
The Hebrew says “to bring you in” and then “to give you their land”; BSB already supplies “their land” as the destination of entering.
The Hebrew uses the image of bringing something back into your heart; BSB says “take to heart.”
The Hebrew speaks of lengthening days and names “your sons”; BSB has “live long” and “your children.”
The Hebrew says “toward the rising of the sun”; BSB condenses this to “to the east.”
The Hebrew says he did not hate the neighbor “yesterday or the day before”; BSB condenses this to “without prior malice.”
The Hebrew joins the final city with “and,” rather than “or,” and uses collective singular names for the three tribal recipients.
The Hebrew says “sons of Israel”; BSB uses “Israelites.”
The Hebrew explicitly says “sons of Israel”; BSB uses “them.”
The Hebrew actively says that Moses and the sons of Israel struck Sihon; BSB makes him the subject of “was defeated.” “The Amorite” is a collective singular.
The Hebrew says “his land,” where BSB names Sihon. It uses collective singular “the Amorite.”
The Hebrew calls Arnon a stream or wadi rather than a valley.
